question: According to material that was officially submitted to the Greek Parliament, Albanian history and geography textbooks, which are also used to teach pupils of the Greek ethnic minority in Northern Epirus, still contain irredentist and revisionist references against Greece1. They show maps in which parts of Greece (e.g. Corfu and parts of Epirus and West Macedonia) are presented as ‘Albanian’.

History chapters contain accounts with references to ‘Chameria’. This raises serious issues concerning respect for the rights of minorities, historical truth and the principles of good neighbourliness, since UNESCO guidelines on textbook revision between neighbouring states and core values of the EU2. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How does it view the Albanian school textbooks containing irredentist material in relation to the accession criteria and the principles of good neighbourliness?
Will it incorporate the findings in question in the annual assessment and in Albania’s EU accession file?

In the context of the cluster 1 (fundamentals) negotiations and in view of the 2026 IBAR assessment, will it ask Albania to set up a joint committee of experts (see UNESCO toolkit for reviewing and adapting curricula, school textbooks and other learning materials) and will it look into whether keeping such references is a reason to suspend accession negotiations in the relevant chapters34?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.6.2026) The Commission attaches great importance to minority rights, education and good neighbourly relations. As part of the accession negotiations, Albania is required to take measures to foster inclusive education, including for persons belonging to minorities.

Albania must uphold educational rights stemming from its law on the Protection of National Minorities, which will have to be fully implemented. Furthermore, the 2025 Enlargement report1 by the Commission sets out that Albania needs to strengthen the quality and inclusiveness of its education system. The Commission will continue monitoring developments related to this field.

The EU common position on Cluster 1: The fundamentals of the accession process sets clear and ambitious interim benchmarks that Albania needs to fulfil to advance in accession negotiations, including protection of rights and rights of persons belonging to minorities, whose education-related issues are assessed and monitored in conjunction with Cluster 3: Competitiveness and inclusive growth.
